newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks maintain uptrend, construction leads.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks maintain uptrend, construction leads.

text.p: Greek shares continued to move higher on Thursday with construction still strong, up 2.74 percent, filtering through to other sectors.
But fund managers said they expected the current wave of appreciation to be short-lived.

"The solid performance in construction is the result of a sudden shift of investor attention to this sector following a period of low trading activity and erosion of prices," said Vasilis Kaloudis, fund manager at International mutual funds.
"But their mini-rally is very fragile because there has been no change in fundamental conditions in the sector," he added.
Low turnover was cited as a further reason for keeping a lid on prices.
"The rise in prices across the board, especially in construction, has been facilitated by a lack of depth in trading activity," he said.
The dollar was fixed at 293.85 drachmas on Thursday, down from Wednesday's all-time high of 295.05 at the Bank of Greece's fixing.
"A higher dollar/drachma exchange rate benefits a large number of blue-chips, especially cement companies, which export in the dollar area," said Kaloudis.
"From a broader prospective, the entire Greek bourse will see larger interest from foreign portfolios as Greek stocks are rendered cheaper by the dollar's climb against the drachma," he added.
The one-month Athibor, Greece's reference interbank rate, eased to 12.08 percent on Thursday from day-earlier 12.13 percent.

"The Bank of Greece's moves to boost liquidity and the prospect of net additions from expiries of funds which will not be rolled-over should help keep short-term rates lower after the recent blip," Kaloudis said.
The Athens benchmark index firmed 1.08 percent or 17.42 points to 1,628.88 from Wednesday's 1,611.46, with construction climbing 2.74 percent.
Industrials and banks were also strong, firming 1.32 and 1.22 percent, respectively.
Turnover reached 12.8 billion drachmas on volume of 3.3 million shares.
